rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Kadid lies between ʿUsfan and Qudayd.
rows.anchor: والكديد ما بين عسفان وقديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ali’s ruling may concern recommended travel, such as visiting virtuous people, or permissible travel for surplus livelihood.
rows.anchor: قد يحتمل أن يحمل قول علي رضي الله عنه ومن وافقه على السفر المندوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For obligatory travel, the traveler need not fast; breaking the fast is preferable for piety, even if he started Ramadan at home, and Qurtubi expects no disagreement.
rows.anchor: ولا يجب عليه الإمساك بل الفطر فيه أفضل للتقوى

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Hanafis require fasting from anyone who enters Ramadan legally competent, neither insane nor unconscious.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: من شهد الشهر بشروط التكليف غير مجنون ولا مغمى عليه فليصمه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: A person insane throughout Ramadan owes no make-up because he did not witness the month in a state that obligates fasting.
rows.anchor: ومن دخل عليه رمضان وهو مجنون وتمادى به طول الشهر فلا قضاء عليه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Someone insane at the beginning and end of Ramadan makes up the days of insanity.
rows.anchor: ومن جن أول الشهر وآخره فإنه يقضي أيام جنونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this interpretation, al-shahr is the explicit direct object of shahida.
rows.anchor: ونصب الشهر على هذا التأويل هو على المفعول الصريح ب «شهد»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation of fasting presupposes Islam, puberty, and knowledge that the month has begun.
rows.anchor: قد تقرر أن فرض الصوم مستحق بالإسلام والبلوغ والعلم بالشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A convert or newly pubescent child before dawn must fast that day; if this occurs after dawn, abstention is recommended, with no make-up for earlier days or that day.
rows.anchor: وإن كان بعد الفجر استحب لهما الإمساك، وليس عليهما قضاء الماضي من الشهر

rows.speaker: مالك والجمهور
rows.claim: A convert owes no make-up for days before conversion because he witnessed Ramadan only after becoming Muslim.
rows.anchor: فقال الإمام مالك والجمهور: ليس عليه قضاء ما مضى لأنه إنما شهد الشهر

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik nevertheless considers it preferable for a convert to make up the day on which he converted.
rows.anchor: قال مالك: وأحب إلي أن يقضي اليوم الذي أسلم فيه

rows.speaker: عطاء والحسن
rows.claim: Ata and al-Hasan say the convert fasts the remainder of Ramadan and makes up the days already passed.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء والحسن: يصوم ما بقي ويقضي ما مضى

rows.speaker: عبد الملك بن الماجشون وأحمد وإسحق
rows.claim: Ibn al-Majishun, Ahmad, and Ishaq require abstaining for the rest of the conversion day and making that day up.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الملك بن الماجشون: يكف عن الأكل في ذلك اليوم ويقضيه. وقال أحمد وإسحق مثله

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says a convert owes neither the past days of Ramadan nor the day of conversion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المنذر: ليس عليه أن يقضي ما مضى من الشهر ولا ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: الباجي
rows.claim: Al-Baji says scholars who hold that non-Muslims are addressed by Islamic law require a convert to abstain for the rest of the day; Ibn Nafi transmits this from Malik, as does Abu al-Qasim.
rows.anchor: وقال الباجي: من قال من أصحابنا أن الكفار مخاطبون بشرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: أشهب وعبد الملك بن الماجشون وابن القاسم
rows.claim: Those who hold non-Muslims are not addressed by Islamic law do not require abstention for the remainder of the day.
rows.anchor: ومن قال من أصحابنا ليسوا مخاطبين قال: لا يلزمه الإمساك في بقية يومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers the view that a convert need not abstain or make up the day: “O believers” addresses believers, not non-Muslims.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهو الصحيح لقوله تعالى: { يأيها الذين آمنوا } فخاطب المؤمنين دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: A group reads al-yusr with a ḍamma on the sīn; it is a dialectal variant, as with al-ʿusr.
rows.anchor: قراءة جماعة «اليسر» بضم السين لغتان، وكذلك «العسر».

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak take ease to mean breaking the fast while traveling and hardship to mean fasting while traveling.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك: «اليسر» الفطر في السفر، و «العسر» الصوم في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the wording is general and covers all matters of religion, citing the denial of hardship in religion.
rows.anchor: والوجه عموم اللفظ في جميع أمور الدين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that God’s religion is easy.
rows.anchor:
وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" دين الله يسر "

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs people to make things easy and not difficult.
rows.anchor:
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" يسروا ولا تعسروا "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusr derives from ease; al-yasār also means wealth.
rows.anchor: واليسر من السهولة، ومنه اليسار للغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The left hand is named either optimistically or because it helps make tasks easier alongside the right hand.
rows.anchor: وسميت اليد اليسرى تفاؤلا، أو لأنه يسهل له الأمر بمعاونتها لليمنى قولان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of hardship restates the affirmation of ease for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { ولا يريد بكم العسر } وهو بمعنى قوله: { يريد الله بكم اليسر }

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Ahl al-Sunna infer that God has an eternal, pre-eternal will additional to His essence, along with eternal attributes of knowledge, power, life, hearing, sight, and speech.
rows.anchor: هذا مذهب أهل السنة كما أنه عالم بعلم

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة والشيعة
rows.claim: Philosophers and Shiʿites deny these attributes; Qurtubi repudiates their position.
rows.anchor: وذهب الفلاسفة والشيعة إلى نفيها تعالى الله عن قول الزائغين وإبطال المبطلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi argues that will is perfection: an agent can choose whether to specify an outcome, while lacking will would be a deficiency.
rows.anchor: فإن من كانت له الصفات الإرادية فله أن يخصص الشيء وله ألا يخصصه فالعقل السليم يقضي بأن ذلك كمال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explicitly describes Himself as willing in several verses, including “Doer of what He wills.”
rows.anchor: وقد وصف نفسه جل جلاله وتقدست أسماؤه بأنه مريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contingent, ordered world must have been specified for existence by an agent who wills, knows, and can create it.
rows.anchor: هذا العالم على غاية من الحكمة والإتقان والانتظام والإحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi argues that willing and power entail life, which entails hearing, sight, and speech; their opposites would imply impossible defects in God.
rows.anchor: وإذ ثبت كونه قادرا مريدا وجب أن يكون حيا إذ الحياة شرط هذه الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is completing the make-up days missed because of illness or travel.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: إكمال عدة الأداء لمن أفطر في سفره أو مرضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is completing the lunar month, whether it has twenty-nine or thirty days.
rows.anchor: الثاني: عدة الهلال سواء كانت تسعا وعشرين أو ثلاثين

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said a lunar month can consist of twenty-nine days.
rows.anchor:
قال جابر بن عبد الله قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إن الشهر يكون تسعا وعشرين "

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority understand the report that the two festival months do not fall short as referring to reward and expiation: either month may have twenty-nine or thirty days.
rows.anchor: وتأوله جمهور العلماء على معنى أنهما لا ينقصان في الأجر وتكفير الخطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Shawwal crescent seen in daylight on Ramadan’s thirtieth day belongs to the coming night, so it does not end that day’s fast.
rows.anchor: ولا اعتبار برؤية هلال شوال يوم الثلاثين من رمضان نهارا بل هو لليلة التي تأتي، هذا هو الصحيح

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A letter attributed to Umar says crescents vary in apparent size and a daytime sighting does not permit breaking the fast unless two witnesses saw it the previous evening.
rows.anchor: إن الأهلة بعضها أكبر من بعض، فإذا رأيتم الهلال نهارا

rows.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن عمر وأنس بن مالك ومالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة ومحمد بن الحسن والليث والأوزاعي وأحمد وإسحق
rows.claim: Abu Umar attributes the same position to Ali, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Umar, Anas, and the listed jurists: the daytime crescent is for the next night.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب مثل ما ذكره عبد الرزاق أيضا، وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر وأنس بن مالك

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: Al-Thawri and Abu Yusuf distinguish by noon: a crescent before noon belongs to the previous night, while one after noon belongs to the next.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري وأبو يوسف: إن رؤي بعد الزوال فهو لليلة التي تأتي

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي
rows.claim: A report from Umar, with a similar report from Ali, says to break the fast if the crescent appears before noon on the thirtieth, but not if it appears after noon.
rows.anchor: إذا رأيتم الهلال نهارا قبل أن تزول الشمس لتمام ثلاثين فأفطروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says no sound isnad is established from Ali on this question.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح في هذه المسألة شيء من جهة الإسناد عن علي

rows.speaker: سليمان بن ربيعة وعبد الملك بن حبيب
rows.claim: Sulayman ibn Rabiʿa and Ibn Habib adopt al-Thawri’s timing rule; Ibn Habib issued fatwas for it in Cordoba.
rows.anchor: وروي عن سليمان بن ربيعة مثل قول الثوري، وإليه ذهب عبد الملك بن حبيب

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Reports differ about Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz’s position on the daylight crescent.
rows.anchor: واختلف عن عمر بن عبد العزيز في هذه المسألة

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar says the connected report from Umar supports Malik’s and the majority’s position; the report supporting al-Thawri is disconnected, and the connected report takes precedence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: والحديث عن عمر بمعنى ما ذهب إليه مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة متصل

rows.speaker: أصحاب قول الثوري
rows.claim: Proponents of al-Thawri’s view argue that al-Aʿmash’s report is general while Ibrahim’s report specifies the timing, so the specific report should govern.
rows.anchor: احتج من ذهب مذهب الثوري بأن قال: حديث الأعمش مجمل لم يخص فيه قبل الزوال ولا بعده

rows.speaker: عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet fasted the thirtieth morning, saw the Shawwal crescent by day, and did not break his fast until evening.
rows.anchor: روته عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: أصبح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صائما

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab says a Shawwal crescent seen from after dawn through sunset belongs to the coming night; Qurtubi calls this agreed upon.
rows.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن المسيب يقول: إن رؤي هلال شوال بعد أن طلع الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the rule that a daytime Shawwal crescent belongs to the coming night is agreed upon.
rows.anchor: وهذا مجمع عليه

rows.speaker: رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: An unnamed Companion reports that two Bedouins testified they had seen the crescent the previous evening; the Prophet ordered people to break the fast and attend the prayer ground the next morning. Al-Daraqutni grades the isnad hasan and established.
rows.anchor: عن ربعي بن حراش عن رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: اختلف الناس

rows.speaker: مالك وأصحابه وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Umar says Malik and his school do not pray Eid on another day or after noon on Eid day, and this position is also reported from Abu Hanifa.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لا خلاف عن مالك وأصحابه أنه لا تصلى صلاة العيد في غير يوم العيد

rows.speaker: الشافعي والمزني
rows.claim: One position of al-Shafiʿi, chosen by al-Muzani, follows Malik: if the prayer is not done after noon on Eid day, the following day is even less suitable.
rows.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي في هذه المسألة فمرة قال بقول مالك، واختاره المزني

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Another reported position of al-Shafiʿi permits Eid prayer on the second morning.
rows.anchor: وعن الشافعي رواية أخرى أنها تصلى في اليوم الثاني ضحى

rows.speaker: البويطي
rows.claim: Al-Buwayti says Eid prayer should be held on the second day only if a hadith establishes that practice.
rows.anchor: وقال البويطي: لا تصلي إلا أن يثبت في ذلك حديث

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar argues that making up Eid prayer after its time would make it resemble an obligatory prayer, whereas the scholars agree other supererogatory prayers are not made up.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لو قضيت صلاة العيد بعد خروج وقتها لأشبهت الفرائض، وقد أجمعوا في سائر السنن

rows.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: Al-Thawri, al-Awzaʿi, Ahmad, and Abu Yusuf permit going out for Eid prayer the next day.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري والأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل: يخرجون من الغد، وقاله أبو يوسف

rows.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn Salih permits a next-day prayer for Eid al-Adha but not Eid al-Fitr.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن صالح بن حي: لا يخرجون في الفطر ويخرجون في الأضحى

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf says the Eid al-Adha prayer may be held for people on the third day.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يوسف: وأما في الأضحى فيصليها بهم في اليوم الثالث

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar explains that Adha has several festival days, while Fitr has only one; if missed, its non-obligatory prayer is not made up.
rows.anchor: لأن الأضحى أيام عيد وهي صلاة عيد، وليس الفطر يوم عيد إلا يوم واحد

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد
rows.claim: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd permits going out the next day for both Fitr and Adha prayers.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث بن سعد: يخرجون في الفطر والأضحى من الغد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi prefers holding Eid prayer the next day because of the established Sunnah, since the Lawgiver may make an exception allowing a Sunnah to be performed after its time.
rows.anchor: قلت: والقول بالخروج إن شاء الله أصح للسنة الثابتة في ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that anyone who missed the two dawn Sunnah rakʿahs may pray them after sunrise; Abu Muhammad authenticates the report, and al-Tirmidhi mentions scholars who act on it.
rows.anchor: من لم يصل ركعتي الفجر فليصلهما بعد ما تطلع الشمس

rows.speaker: الترمذي والثوري والشافعي وأحمد وإسحق وابن المبارك
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi says some scholars act on this report, naming al-Thawri, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Ibn al-Mubarak; Umar is also reported to have done so.
rows.anchor: قال الترمذي: والعمل على هذا عند بعض أهل العلم، وبه يقول سفيان الثوري والشافعي

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Maliki scholars say someone who prayed dawn because time was short may pray the omitted dawn Sunnah after sunrise if he wishes; another view forbids it.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: من ضاق عليه الوقت وصلى الصبح وترك ركعتي الفجر

rows.speaker: الشيخ أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr says treating those two rakʿahs as make-up follows the school’s principle, though calling them qada is loose usage.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو بكر: وهذا الجاري على أصل المذهب، وذكر القضاء تجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says next-day Fitr prayer may likewise be allowed after its time, especially because it occurs only once yearly and the Sunnah establishes it.
rows.anchor: قلت: ولا يبعد أن يكون حكم صلاة الفطر في اليوم الثاني على هذا الأصل

rows.speaker: أبو عمير بن أنس عن عمومة له
rows.claim: Anas’s uncles report that people who saw the crescent came to the Prophet; he ordered them to break the fast once the day had advanced and go to the Eid prayer the next day.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمير بن أنس عن عمومة له: أن قوما رأوا الهلال فأتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمرهم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو والحسن وقتادة والأعرج
rows.claim: Abu Bakr’s transmission from ʿAsim, one report from Abu ʿAmr, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Aʿraj read tukammilū with a doubled mīm.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في بعض ما روي عنه والحسن وقتادة والأعرج { ولتكملوا العدة } بالتشديد

rows.speaker: الباقون والكسائي
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the un-doubled form; al-Kisaʾi prefers it, comparing it with “Today I completed your religion.”
rows.anchor: والباقون بالتخفيف. واختار الكسائي التخفيف

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the two forms are dialects with the same meaning, as in the paired forms in 86:17.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: وهما لغتان بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is not read with a vowelless lām; the Basran analysis supplies an understood أن after the purpose lām.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز «ولتكملوا» بإسكان اللام

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basran grammarians parse the lām as introducing a purpose clause, estimated as “He wills that you complete”; they disallow deleting أن and its vowel.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز حذف أن والكسرة هذا قول البصريين

rows.speaker: كثير أبو صخر
rows.claim: The poetic phrase “I wish to forget her memory” is cited to show the construction لِأَنْسى, with أن after the lām.
rows.anchor: قول كثير أبو صخر: أريد لأنسى ذكرها أي لأن أنسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says this lām can introduce an object, as in “I struck for Zayd,” so the sense is that God intends completion of the number.
rows.anchor: وهذه اللام هي الداخلة على المفعول كالتي في قولك: ضربت لزيد

rows.speaker: الكوفيون والفراء
rows.claim: The Kufans, as al-Farraʾ relates, attach the lām to an implicit later verb: God granted this concession so that people may complete the number; al-Nahhas calls this a good analysis.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الكوفيين وحكاه النحاس عن الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction is compared to 6:75, where showing Abraham the kingdom of heaven and earth was done so he would be among the certain.
rows.anchor: وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت السماوات والأرض وليكون من الموقنين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation treats the waw as superfluous.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الواو مقحمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the lām imperative, with the waw coordinating one sentence to another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن تكون هذه اللام لام الأمر والواو عاطفة جملة كلام

rows.speaker: أبو إسحق إبراهيم بن السري
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq interprets the wording by its meaning: God did this to make matters easy and so people would complete the number.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق إبراهيم بن السري: هو محمول على المعنى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s cited couplet supplies an implicitly repeated phrase, illustrating the ellipsis proposed in this construction.
rows.anchor: ومشجج أما سواء قذاله فبدا وغيب ساره المعزاء

rows.speaker: جمهور أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The majority of exegetes take the clause as urging magnification of God at the end of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولتكبروا الله } عطف عليه، ومعناه الحض على التكبير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وعروة وأبو سلمة
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi reports that Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa, and Abu Salama would say takbir and praise God on the night of Fitr, by analogy with the night of Adha.
rows.anchor: روي عن سعيد ابن المسيب وعروة وأبي سلمة أنهم كانوا يكبرون ليلة الفطر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muslims must say takbir upon seeing the Shawwal crescent.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: حق على المسلمين إذا رأوا هلال شوال أن يكبروا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas places takbir from sighting the crescent through the sermon, pausing when the imam comes out and joining his takbir.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه: يكبر المرء من رؤية الهلال إلى انقضاء الخطبة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say takbir begins with sighting the crescent and ends when the imam comes out for prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: يكبر من رؤية الهلال إلى خروج الإمام للصلاة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan says the takbir is said on the day of Fitr.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان: هو التكبير يوم الفطر

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم ومالك
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says takbir runs from setting out for the prayer ground until prayer ends; Malik’s school places it from leaving home until the imam comes out.
rows.anchor: زيد بن أسلم: يكبرون إذا خرجوا إلى المصلى فإذا انقضت الصلاة انقضى العيد

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم وعلي بن زياد
rows.claim: Malik’s transmitters say one leaving before sunrise does not say takbir en route or while waiting until sunrise; one leaving later says it en route and while waiting for the imam.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن القاسم وعلي بن زياد: أنه إن خرج قبل طلوع الشمس فلا يكبر

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi apply the same takbir practice to Fitr and Adha.
rows.anchor: والفطر والأضحى في ذلك سواء عند مالك، وبه قال الشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires takbir for Adha but not Fitr.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: يكبر في الأضحى ولا يكبر في الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi invokes the command to magnify God and the annual Fitr celebration in support of takbir at Fitr.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى: { ولتكبروا الله } ولأن هذا يوم عيد لا يتكرر في العام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reports that people were more emphatic about takbir at Fitr than at Adha.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال: كانوا في التكبير في الفطر أشد منهم في الأضحى

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the Prophet said takbir from leaving home until reaching the prayer ground on Fitr.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكبر يوم الفطر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar himself would loudly say takbir on Fitr and Adha while going out, continuing until the imam arrived.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر: أنه كان إذا غدا يوم الأضحى ويوم الفطر يجهر بالتكبير

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم وابن المنذر والأوزاعي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says most early Muslims and scholars held takbir at Fitr; al-Awzaʿi transmitted this from Ilyas.
rows.anchor: وأكثر أهل العلم على التكبير في عيد الفطر من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi favors communal and individual takbir from the Shawwal crescent until setting out and when the imam comes to pray, and likewise on Adha night for non-pilgrims.
rows.anchor: وكان الشافعي يقول إذا رأى هلال شوال: أحببت أن يكبر الناس جماعة وفرادى

rows.speaker: مالك وجماعة من العلماء
rows.claim: Malik and a group of scholars use three repetitions of “Allahu akbar”; this wording is also reported from Jabir ibn Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: ولفظ التكبير عند مالك وجماعة من العلماء: الله أكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر، ثلاثا

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars mix takbir with declarations of divine oneness and glorification, while others use the longer formula “Allahu akbar kabira …”.
rows.anchor: ومن العلماء من يكبر ويهلل ويسبح أثناء التكبير. ومنهم من يقول: الله أكبر كبيرا

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak’s Fitr formula includes takbir, the testimony of oneness, praise, and “God is greatest for guiding us.”
rows.anchor: وكان ابن المبارك يقول إذا خرج من يوم الفطر: الله أكبر الله أكبر، لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر وأحمد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says Malik set no fixed formula or limit; Ahmad calls the practice broad.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وكان مالك لا يحد فيه حدا. وقال أحمد: هو واسع

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says his scholars choose unrestricted takbir as the Qurʾan’s apparent sense; Qurtubi inclines to that view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «واختار علماؤنا التكبير المطلق، وهو ظاهر القرآن وإليه أميل»

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation links the praise to Christians’ error in changing their fast.
rows.anchor: قيل: لما ضل فيه النصارى من تبديل صيامهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation contrasts divine guidance with the pagan custom of boasting about ancestors, lineage, and accomplishments.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بدلا عما كانت الجاهلية تفعله من التفاخر بالآباء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A broader explanation is to magnify God for guiding people to the religious laws.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لتعظموه على ما أرشدكم إليه من الشرائع فهو عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi refers readers back to his earlier explanation of “so that you may be grateful.”
rows.anchor: وتقدم معنى { ولعلكم تشكرون }

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the rites are sacrificial animals and the shedding of blood.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: المناسك الذبائح وهراقة الدماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the rites as the ceremonies of Hajj, supported by the Prophet’s instruction to learn the rites from him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي شعائر الحج لقوله عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After performing a Hajj rite, people should remember God and praise Him for His blessings.
rows.anchor: المعنى: فإذا فعلتم منسكا من مناسك الحج فاذكروا الله

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the first kāf into the second in manāsikakum because the consonants are identical.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو يدغم الكاف في الكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here qaḍaytum means that the rites were performed and completed, as in the usage for performing Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: و «قضيتم» هنا بمعنى أديتم وفرغتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qaḍāʾ can also describe worship performed outside its prescribed time.
rows.anchor: وقد يعبر بالقضاء عما فعل من العبادات خارج وقتها المحدود لها

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority say Arabs used to boast at the Jamra after Hajj about ancestral valor and generosity and ask for worldly blessings like their fathers’; the verse requires more remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: كانت عادة العرب إذا قضت حجها تقف عند الجمرة، فتفاخر بالآباء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabiʿ interpret the phrase as children’s remembrance of parents: seek God’s aid as children once sought their parents.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع: معنى الآية واذكروا الله كذكر الأطفال آبائهم

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says to exalt God, defend His sanctuary, and repel those who would introduce polytheism, as people defend and praise their ancestors.
rows.anchor: وقالت طائفة: معنى الآية اذكروا الله وعظموه وذبوا عن حرمه

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وابن عباس
rows.claim: When Abu al-Jawza asked why the verse matters if people no longer mention their fathers, Ibn Abbas replied that anger at God’s disobedience should exceed anger at an insult to one’s parents.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الجوزاء لابن عباس: إن الرجل اليوم لا يذكر أباه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the kāf phrase as an accusative verbal noun: “remembrance like your remembrance.”
rows.anchor: والكاف من قوله { كذكركم } في موضع نصب أي ذكرا كذكركم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says aw ashadd may be genitive, coordinated with dhikrikum and meaning “or like stronger remembrance”; because it is an afʿal adjective, it is not declined.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: «أو أشد» في موضع خفض عطفا على ذكركم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, aw ashadd is accusative, meaning “remember Him more strongly”; dhikran is accusative as specification.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بمعنى أو اذكروه أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is nominative as the subject, or may be adjectival; “says, Our Lord…” is its relative clause.
rows.anchor: «من» في موضع رفع بالابتداء، وإن شئت بالصفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described as making only this worldly supplication are polytheists.
rows.anchor: والمراد المشركون

rows.speaker: أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: Abu Waʾil, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd say pre-Islamic Arabs prayed only for worldly goods such as livestock and victory, since they did not know or believe in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد: كانت العرب في الجاهلية تدعوا في مصالح الدنيا فقط

words: وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the warning may also apply to a believer who restricts supplication to worldly matters; “no share” means no share like the one who asks for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتناول هذا الوعيد المؤمن أيضا إذا قصر دعواته في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalaq means a share, and min is extra in the construction; Qurtubi notes that this was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: والخلاق النصيب. و «من» زائدة وقد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioners about wine and gambling are believers, as Qurtubi noted earlier.
rows.anchor: السائلون هم المؤمنون كما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr is named from khamara, “to cover”: it veils the intellect, just as a woman’s veil covers and anything covering something is said to khammar it.
rows.anchor: والخمر مأخوذة من خمر إذا ستر ومنه خمار المرأة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The unnamed poet’s phrase khamr al-tariq refers to a hollow or depression that conceals a wolf or other creature.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: ألا يا زيد والضحاك سيرا فقد جاوزتما خمر الطريق

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj’s phrase al-khamr describes someone who does not move concealed, illustrating the sense of hiding.
rows.anchor: وقال العجاج يصف جيشا يمشي برايات وجيوش غير مستخف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ghimār or khimār of people can mean a hidden place or a place within the crowd.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم: دخل في غمار الناس وخمارهم أي هو في مكان خاف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second etymology connects khamr with being left to mature, as dough ferments or an opinion is left to become clear.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها تركت حتى أدركت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third etymology derives the name from mixing with the intellect, from mukhāmarah, “mixing.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها تخالط العقل، من المخامرة وهي المخالطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the three explanations converge: wine matures, mixes with the intellect, then covers it; concealment is the root sense.
rows.anchor: فالمعاني الثلاثة متقاربة فالخمر تركت وخمرت حتى أدركت، ثم خالطت العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine is grape juice that ferments or is cooked; any other substance that intoxicates the intellect has the same legal status.
rows.anchor: والخمر: ماء العنب الذي غلى أو طبخ وما خامر العقل من غيره فهو في حكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi extends the prohibition to all gambling by consensus, since maysir originally concerned wagering on camels; by the same analogy, other intoxicants take wine’s ruling.
rows.anchor: لأن إجماع العلماء أن القمار كله حرام

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority hold that any drink whose large quantity intoxicates is forbidden in both small and large quantities, and that the prescribed penalty applies.
rows.anchor: والجمهور من الأمة على أن ما أسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب فمحرم قليله وكثيره

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وفقهاء الكوفة
rows.claim: These Kufan jurists allow small amounts of non-grape drinks that intoxicate in large amounts and deny the penalty absent deliberate intoxication; Qurtubi calls this weak and rejects it by reason and transmitted evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وجماعة من فقهاء الكوفة: ما أسكر كثيره

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say God bestowed every honor and good on this community and prescribed laws gradually rather than all at once; wine prohibition likewise came in stages.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: إن الله تعالى لم يدع شيئا من الكرامة والبر إلا أعطاه هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says this verse was the first revelation on wine; the later stages are detailed in the following segment.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية أول ما نزل في أمر الخمر، ثم بعده:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi places the prohibition on approaching prayer while intoxicated at the next stage of the wine rulings.
rows.anchor:
لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى
[النساء: 43]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He next cites the verse explaining that Satan uses wine and gambling to sow hostility and obstruct remembrance and prayer.
rows.anchor: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He then cites the command to avoid wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows as satanic impurity.
rows.anchor: إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir originally means the Arabs’ gambling with arrows.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والميسر } الميسر: قمار العرب بالأزلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a pre-Islamic man wagered his family and property; the winner took the loser’s wealth and family, and the verse was revealed about this.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر الرجل على أهله وماله

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومحمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن المسيب وعطاء وقتادة ومعاوية بن صالح وطاوس وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: These authorities define maysir broadly as anything involving gambling, including dice, chess, and children’s games with walnuts or knucklebones, except permitted horse wagers and lotteries for allocating rights.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومحمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن المسيب وعطاء وقتادة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik divides maysir into amusement, including dice, chess, and entertainments, and gambling involving wagers.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: الميسر ميسران: ميسر اللهو

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali calls chess “the maysir of the non-Arabs.”
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب: الشطرنج ميسر العجم

rows.speaker: مالك وجماعة العلماء
rows.claim: Malik and other scholars treat anything wagered upon as maysir.
rows.anchor: وكل ما قومر به فهو ميسر عند مالك وغيره من العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maysir derives from yusr: it is something that becomes due to its owner; yāsir is the player with the arrows.
rows.anchor: والميسر مأخوذ من اليسر، وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line “fa-aʿinhum wa-aysir…” uses a form from y-s-r for playing the arrows or taking part in maysir.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فأعنهم وايسر بما يسروا به

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says maysir can name the camel gambled over because it is divided into shares; anything divided is described with the same root.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الميسر: الجزور الذي كانوا يتقامرون عليه سمي ميسرا لأنه يجزأ أجزاء

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says yāsir originally means the butcher who portions the camel; by extension it names the arrow players and gamblers who cause the slaughter.
rows.anchor: والياسر: الجازر لأنه يجزىء لحم الجزور

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Sihah records that “the people yasara the camel” means they slaughtered it and divided its portions.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح: ويسر القوم الجزور أي اجتزروها واقتسموا أعضاءها
